title: No sober quarrel over removing images; Luther would rather not set them in the temple
pass_a_gloss: There is NO quarrel stirred by the Leipzigers, or the Rinteln men, or other more clear-headed Lutherans, about the images removed among the Reformed. None appear either in most of their churches. That it is even more useful that none be placed on Altars or in Temples, Luther long ago laid down — whatever he disapproved in the impulsive Iconoclasts led on at first by Karlstadt, without any authority of the Magistrate: "Otherwise," he says, "I do not greatly love Images, and I would wish them not to be set up in the Temple" (Annotations on Deuteronomy, Jena Latin, vol. III, fol. 99). The same was felt by the Wittenberg theologians, the Giessen men, Nic. Palladius the Copenhagen theologian, David Chytraeus, Martin Chemnitz, and others. See the testimonies in Christoph. Massonius, Universal Anatomy of Germany against Matth. Hoe, Part III, from p. 404.
pass_b_english: No quarrel worth the name has been raised by the Leipzigers, the Rinteln men, or other more sober Lutherans over the images the Reformed have taken down. In most of those churches none appear either.
Luther himself long ago judged it more useful that none stand on altars or in temples — whatever he blamed in the hotheaded iconoclasts first led on by Karlstadt without the magistrate's authority.
"Otherwise," he says, "I do not greatly love images, and I would rather they were not set up in the temple" (Annotations on Deuteronomy, Jena Latin, vol. III, fol. 99).

Wittenberg and Giessen theologians, Nic. Palladius of Copenhagen, David Chytraeus, Martin Chemnitz, and others felt the same. Massonius gathers the testimonies against Matth. Hoe (Universal Anatomy of Germany, Part III, from p. 404).
source_text: NULLA de summotis inter Reformatos Imaginibus, lis mota à Lipsiacis, vel Rintelensibus nec cordatioribus aliis inter Lutheranos. Nullae etiam apparent in plurimis eorum Ecclesiis. Utilius etiam esse, nullas in Altaribus aut Templis collocari, pridem Lutherus statuit, quicquid impetuosos Iconoclastas inductu primo Carolostadii, nulla auctoritate Magistratus, improbaret: Alias, ego (inquit) Imagines non admodum amo, & vellem in Templo non statui, Annot. in Deuter. T. III. Jen. Lat. fol. 99. Idem senserunt Theologi Wittenbergenses, Giessenses, Nic. Palladius Hafniensis Theologus, Dav. Chytraeus, Mart. Chemnitius, &c. Testimonia videsis apud Christoph. Massonium, Anat. Universalis German. contra Matth. Hoë, P. III. à pag. 404.
